html:
Laguneros, "lake people", was the Spanish name for the peoples of the Laguna region of Coahuila and Durango, in northern Mexico. Most of them were the Irritila.

They lived around shallow lakes fed by the Nazas and Aguanaval rivers, fishing and gathering. Jesuit missionaries reached them around 1594, and the mission town of Parras was founded in 1598. Disease and Spanish settlement broke up their bands within a century, and the lakes themselves were later drained for cotton farms. Their neighbours to the north were the Toboso.
sum: Laguneros, "lake people", was the Spanish name for the peoples of the Laguna region of Coahuila and Durango, in northern Mexico. Most of them were the Irritila.
